messages.content: Write the introduction to a guide for a REST API that manages calendar bookings. Around 200 words.

The Calendar Bookings API enables applications to manage time-based reservations programmatically. Whether you're building a scheduling platform, integrating booking capabilities into an existing application, or automating appointment workflows, this API provides a complete set of endpoints to create, retrieve, update, and cancel bookings.

The API follows REST conventions and uses JSON for request and response bodies. All communication occurs over HTTPS with API key authentication in request headers.

Key capabilities include creating bookings with customizable time slots and metadata, querying available time windows to prevent double-bookings, modifying existing reservations, and canceling bookings with optional notification triggers. The API supports pagination for listing operations and webhooks for real-time updates when bookings change. Responses include consistent status codes and error messages to help you handle edge cases reliably.

Before making requests, you'll need an API key from your dashboard. Every endpoint requires authentication, and requests are rate-limited to prevent abuse. Response headers include information on cache behavior and rate-limit status.

This guide covers authentication, available endpoints, request and response formats, error handling, and common use cases. Code examples are provided in popular languages, and a sandbox environment lets you test integrations before deploying to production.

The Calendar Bookings API lets you manage time-based reservations programmatically. Automate scheduling across your platform.

Build scheduling platforms, add booking capabilities to existing applications, or streamline appointment workflows. This API provides endpoints to create, retrieve, update, and cancel bookings—everything you need to run a booking system.

The API uses REST conventions and JSON for all payloads. Communication happens over HTTPS with API key authentication in request headers. Key capabilities include creating bookings with customizable time slots and metadata, querying available time windows to prevent double-bookings, modifying existing reservations, and canceling bookings with optional notification triggers. The API also supports pagination for listing operations, webhooks for real-time updates when bookings change, and consistent status codes and error messages for reliable edge-case handling.

Before you start, get an API key from your dashboard. Every endpoint requires authentication, and requests are rate-limited to prevent abuse.

This guide walks through authentication, endpoints, request and response formats, and error handling strategies. We've included code examples in popular languages and provided access to a sandbox environment for testing before production deployment.
